newsitem.title: USA: Switching polio vaccines costly, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Switching polio vaccines costly, study finds.

text.p: Switching completely to an inactivated polio virus for vaccinations in the United States would not be cost effective but could be justified from a public health standpoint, a study said Tuesday.

The naturally occurring, or "wild," polio virus has been eradicated in the Western Hemisphere. The live but weakened polio vaccine currently in use in the United States, however, carries a slight risk of causing polio, although only a handful of such cases occur each year.

An advisory committee to the U.S. Public Health Service has recommended adoption of a half-and-half vaccination programme, consisting of two inactivated virus vaccinations followed by two with the live virus.

Researchers at the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, in a study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association, said it would cost $28 million more per year to switch completely to an inactivated vaccine, while a mix of the two would cost only $14.7 million more.
The figures are beyond the estimated $11 million that would be saved by not having to pay compensation to those who get the disease from the live vaccine.

Switching completely to the inactive vaccine "would not be cost-beneficial at current vaccine prices and with the current compensation awards paid to vaccine-associated paralytic (polio) cases," the report said.

"Although these figures are greater than those for many other public health programmes, they may be justified to assuage public concerns about adverse events associated with a government-mandated oral polio vaccine programme in the United States, where there is no disease due to wild poliovirus," it added.

"Continued public confidence in poliomyelitis vaccination programmes is essential to ensure the high vaccination coverage necessary to prevent epidemic transmission of imported wild poliovirus," the study said.

"In addition, public confidence in the safety of vaccination programmes in general may provide the additional benefit of higher vaccine coverage and more effective prevention of all childhood diseases preventable by vaccine," it said.
